reviews.title: Cute UI, bad GPS
reviews.text:
I started using the app because they didn’t change the names of Lake Ontario and the Gulf of Mexico. I like to look and the way that the UI works, I especially adore being able to make my avatar a unicorn. 

Unfortunately, the most important part of the experience is severely lacking, which is correct and accurate locations and directions. On average, 50% of the destinations that I enter are listed in the wrong place on the map. Also, the process of reporting incorrect locations is unnecessarily cumbersome; the separate website you report issues on requires you to find the latitude and longitude on a separate page and then enter it in and the page is constantly refreshed when you click away so nothing is actually kept when you go to get the lat/long. Other apps allow you to just report through the app, and that is a huge miss on this one. I wish I could use it, I would really love to get behind it. Unfortunately, it’s more important that I actually get where I’m going when using a navigation application, and the fact that it really can’t be improved much with the current reporting system is a dealbreaker.

reviews.title: I SO want to like this app…
reviews.text:
Like many, disgust with the bootlicking sycophants at Google and Apple led me to this app (and a huge “bravo” to its leaders for refusing to bend the knee), but alas, it’s just not ready for primetime yet. 

As others have noted, it often gives directions that defy common sense (twice it’s tried to have me take a highway then exit and loop back, when the surface street I was on went directly to my destination). More critically, it does not have any inputs for real-time user updates, such as stalled cars, objects on the road, heavy traffic, accidents, and police presence. Without that 21st century interactivity, this app is nothing more than a screen version of a paper map, forcing you to interpret the way forward and hope for the best. 

It is my sincere hope that the developers will be motivated by their product’s current moment in the spotlight to update and release a version that works the way that their competitors do. That would be a product that I, and likely many more, would endorse and use. Otherwise, it will remain a quaint remnant of the early internet, when 8-bit graphics was considered cutting edge technology.

reviews.title: I wanted to like it!
reviews.text:
I so wanted to love MapQuest. The unicorn is whimsical, I appreciate the company’s stance, and the directions themselves were clear and easy to follow. However, a few things held me back from fully switching over.

The biggest issue was that MapQuest wasn’t very good at identifying my current location, which made getting started more frustrating than it should have been. I also found that some key locations were missing from the map entirely, with it attempting to send me to a different state. A few times, I wound up opening Google Maps just to look up the location I was trying to navigate to, which felt pretty counterproductive when I was specifically trying to use MapQuest instead.

There’s a lot I like here, and I really wanted it to become my go-to navigation app, but those basic functionality gaps made it hard to rely on.

reviews.title: Needs a Lot of Work for 2026
reviews.text: I switched to this app after Apple changed Lake Ontario’s name. The map doesn’t change from dark to light in the daylight. The voiced step-by-step directions are nice, but when you have to change your route due to roadwork, the app doesn’t reroute for you. I had to go a few miles out of my way to get to a different on-ramp. The app continued to try to route me back to the road construction. In fact, I was a few miles away from that route, and it wasn’t until I was 1500 feet from the next ramp that it accepted that I wasn’t going to turn around and go back. If I were in an unfamiliar area and that happened, I’d simply be lost, and have to pull over and stop to move the map around on my phone (my car screen isn’t touch screen) until I could try and find a way to get to my destination. And since the map is dark in the daylight, I’d have to keep looking at my phone to see the map. That’s just dangerous.

reviews.title: Helpful but needs help
reviews.text: I really want to like this app! It needs better Apple Maps integration with a dedicated sound button on screen to choose levels of direction and alert capabilities. I don’t want to hear turn by turn directions but I do want to know if there is a road hazard, new route suggestion or police ahead. It also needs a dedicated home and work button so you don’t have to press search, then favorites and then home. Also, the volume function needs help as well. You need to have the option to mute audio while it’s giving directions or lower audio. It would also be nice to report police and road hazards. The characters are fun, but them standing off to the side of the road can lead to confusion when you are starting a new route because you don’t know if you are on the road, you’re supposed to be on or not. Also, when you get to your destination, it needs to clearly state if you are supposed to be arriving on the left-hand or right hand side of the road because it does not clearly indicate so when you arrive at your destination. I am a long time user of Google Maps and Waze, and have noticed that MapQuest routes are not always the best. And seem to favor only major roadways. Multiple times I have looked at the routes and they have not made logical sense. However, I really like the values of the company so I am willing to stick it out if these changes can eventually be made!

reviews.title: Needs work
reviews.text:
I’d love to make the switch from Google Maps, but this app has a long way to go before I can.

First, the feedback button is broken in the app, so I need to write a review here instead. Second, turn-by-turn directions are played as music while muting your whatever you have playing. There is no option to play it as navigation, which has its own volume to control in most cars. Third, directions are poor, often telling me to drive around non-existent traffic or closures, adding 5-10 minutes to my normal commutes. Lastly, it’s more of an annoyance but it sends a notification every single time you connect to CarPlay. I don’t always need or want to get directions anywhere, so this just adds irritation.

Great start, but there’s loads of work to be done to compete with other more fleshed out options.

reviews.title: wrong addresses
reviews.text: i’m noticing that there are restaurants in the wrong places, and when you click on them, they are listed as the correct street address, but on the map they are clearly in the wrong place. Not even close.  So you have a restaurant on the opposite side of town when they should be located in somewhere else.  There is no report feature to report that they are in the wrong place so I don’t know how to help improve it.  I’m concerned that if I’m not familiar with the area that I would end up driving to the wrong place.  How is it that something that’s labeled as having an address of State Street physically located on the map on Washington Avenue…. It’s like the data is correct but it’s just representing in the wrong spot.  I was assuming there would be some issues with not as many known locations, but having locations with the correct address and just literally in the wrong spot on the map is odd.  I tested out getting directions and surely enough the directions are to the wrong place on the map.  If I use MapQuest, I will be getting lost and I don’t know if I have the stomach or patience for that.

reviews.title: Are you kidding?
reviews.text: My app updated when I got my new phone. Talk about culture shock! The new format is anything but intuitive. How do I need collections? I’d rather see a list of favorites, places I visit often enough, but not often enough to be able to go right to them without MapQuest. Those useful shortcuts are in one line that I have to scroll through. In the old MapQuest, there was a nice list. I could see quite a few of them at a glance. I have yet to figure out how to get rid of the collections. The old MapQuest showed all your trip options right after you search. Now to get to your options, you choose directions. That used to be for just figuring out the distance between places. No, there’s no intuitiveness here. I don’t even like the look of it. And I’m paying a premium each month. I would like to have my old MapQuest, which I had recommended many times. I do not recommend or like or appreciate the new MapQuest. In fact, it’s a pain. I wish there was at least some option to have some of the old features. Old school and new school do not like the same things. Is that OK? 😡
